THE NEW INDIA
THE MODERN INTER-CULTURAL WEDDING DRESS CODE
 
In an age of noise, Sabyasachi chooses silence, intention over conformity, and substance over spectacle.
This is not bridal wear for performance. It’s a refusal to conform. It ignores trends and refutes that tradition must be loud to be appreciated.
Lehengas, rich with craft, are paired with quiet dupattas so the embroidery can breathe. The styling is spare; jewellery edited; every detail essential. She chooses with discernment and wears heritage as presence, not performance.
In the New India, maximalism and minimalism meet like memory and intention. A balance. A tightrope above the stereotypical. As brides declare for themselves who they are; when they seek truth over validation, they become a catalyst for change. As Sabyasachi has always said: “For heritage to be relevant, it must be dynamic.”

THE NEW WORLD
THE MODERN MULTICULTURAL WEDDING DRESS CODE
 
In love, everything becomes ancestral. This collection is about heritage in motion.
 
As more Indian men and women find love across continents, cultures, and genders, I find myself drawn to the quiet transformations taking place inside weddings. Cross-cultural unions are entering Indian tradition with humility.
 
“The New World” is my response to this moment: a bridal collection that leans into traditional silhouettes but is stripped of excess. The jewellery is edited, deliberate. The fabrics are still opulent, but the styling is more nuanced. The dupattas are lighter, sometimes even translucent. There is a dignity in their weightlessness.
 
This is not a dilution of culture; it is refinement. For these couples, their choices speak of initiation, not appropriation, presence over performance. Occidental preference to edit has found harmony with the oriental instinct to ornament. This is India; not inherited but chosen, which is the most modern act of all.

“I have never believed that a luxury store should simply sell products. It should inspire curiosity, preserve culture and create memory. Commerce may bring people through the door, but culture is what makes them return.” 
— Sabyasachi Mukherjee

For nearly two decades, Sabyasachi stores have been built on a simple belief: Indian luxury deserves spaces that express its identity, craftsmanship and culture with confidence.

As the world becomes increasingly digital, that purpose becomes even clearer: to create something tangible — a place to discover heritage, encounter craft and experience the human connection that defines luxury.

The new Sabyasachi New Delhi flagship spans over 26,000 sq. ft., more than doubling its original footprint, and debuting a dedicated High Jewellery salon and accessory parlour.

Inspired by the romance of luxury train travel, labyrinthine corridors dense with curiosities bring together 120 chandeliers, nearly 200 antique carpets, 300 original paintings by the Sabyasachi Art Foundation, and more than 100 antique textiles, mirrors and decorative objects.

Lavish mother-of-pearl inlay, pink Sarrancolin marble, life-sized statues and a bespoke installation inspired by the tramcars of Calcutta transform the store into a living museum and cultural destination, complete with an immersive playlist curated by Sabyasachi Mukherjee and Bengali tea rituals.

Mehrauli, New Delhi 110030 
 
Opening on 25th August 2026

She fell in love with everything.
The first sip of chai in the morning. Rain tapping against the window. Books with folded corners. People who laughed with their whole heart.
Every time something made her smile, a tiny red heart appeared on her.
One became two. Two became twenty.
Soon, she was covered in little reminders that love isn’t rare at all. It’s everywhere, if you remember to notice it.
That’s how she became Safed Ishq.
Soft as a blank page, carrying tiny embroidered hearts like secrets only the observant can find. She doesn’t believe love needs a reason. She simply believes there’s always room for one more little heart.

Love doesn’t always arrive with grand gestures. Sometimes, it lingers in little moments, a shared smile, a handwritten note, or a heart doodled in the corner of a page. Safed Ishq celebrates exactly that. Crafted from Suta’s signature feather-soft mul cotton in a serene white, this borderless saree is scattered with tiny embroidered red hearts, adding a playful touch to an otherwise understated drape. Light, breathable, and full of charm, it’s a saree that wears its heart with quiet confidence.

title: Things no one tells you about styling curly hair… but I will 👀
body_text:
1. Style in the shower. Hair should be dripping, not “damp”. My in shower lighting isn’t good, so I do it in the room, only for you

2. Fresh wash only. No conditioner = tangles + frizz.

3. If it starts drying while styling → add more water.

4. Go easy on leave-in/curl cream. Coat, don’t overload.

5. Always follow with a gel. Cream alone isn’t enough.

6. Don’t touch your hair while it dries. Just leave it alone.

7. Flipping? Don’t be aggressive. Slow head shakes > chaos.

8. Skip full-speed hairdryer. Diffuser if needed, but air dry > heat.

9. In a rush? Diffuse gently, low speed.

10. Once dry, scrunch out the gel cast with a little oil/serum. (Cast = good, don’t panic)
